title: Author the GitHub Actions workflow that deploys Fabric artifacts via fabric-cicd on merge to main
description: Write the GitHub Actions workflow that installs fabric-cicd, authenticates as the Service Principal from repository secrets, and publishes the fabric/ artifact definitions to the workspace on merge to main. Deployment logic only — secret configuration and the first live run are task-046.
acceptanceCriteria: A workflow at .github/workflows/deploy-fabric.yml triggers on push to main and supports manual dispatch.
It authenticates via Service Principal using repository secrets, never inline credentials.
It invokes fabric-cicd against fabric/ using the parameter.yml from task-044.
The workflow is inspectable as a dry run — a mode that resolves and reports what would deploy without publishing.
Workflow YAML is syntactically valid (verified locally, e.g. via actionlint or an equivalent parse check).
notes: CREATED 2026-07-29 by /work task-spec coherence audit. Spec § Next Steps & Priorities defines Phase 4 (CI/CD Deployment) with concrete deliverables, but the project had zero Phase 4 tasks — verified by a grep probe with a positive control. This task is part of the 4-task set that closes that coverage gap.
Spec anchor: § Next Steps & Priorities → Phase 4 deliverable 1, 'Deployment triggered on merge to main'.
SEQUENCING: authored before task-043 completes is fine — this task writes the workflow; task-046 supplies the secrets and proves it runs.

HAZARD: this deploys INTO the live workspace Erik works in via the Fabric UI. The dry-run mode in criterion 4 exists so the first execution cannot clobber in-flight UI work. Confirm commit ordering (Fabric -> local -> Update) still holds under an automated pusher before the first real deploy.
